newsitem.title: USA: Intel posts sharp profit, sales gains in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Intel posts sharp profit, sales gains in quarter.

text.p: Intel Corp. Monday reported sharply higher third-quarter profits, reflecting solid demand for its Pentium microprocessor.

The world's largest semiconductor maker earned $1.3 billion, or $1.48 a share, in the three months ended in September, up from $931 million, or $1.05 a share, a year ago. Revenues rose 23 percent to $5.14 billion.
The results stunned Wall Street, which had expected Intel to post a gain equal to $1.25 a share, and in after-hours trading, Intel's stock surged $4.375 to $112.

During the period, which ended Sept. 28, shipments of microprocessors and chipsets set a record. In addition, its book-to-bill ratio was greater than 1.0, an indication that new orders exceeded shipments, Intel said.

Widely regarded as a bellwether for the technology industry, Intel had raised expectations last month when it told investors third-quarter revenues would be above the $4.62 billion reported in the second quarter.

Intel has benefited from the strong acceptance of its Pentium and Pentium Pro microprocessors -- the powerful computer chips that enable users to operate a wide variety of programmes at the same time.
